GB-3 is not met because the line is straight, on the centre line, has no bright edge, and there is no second light or raking view. candidates.hypothesis: Expected mold seam (centre-line, straight, even width) vs. crack: the line sits at x~0.5 and is straight, so GB-1 applies if it also appears on the approved reference.

proposed_action.expected_evidence: If the line is the expected mold seam, the reference image shows the same vertical line at x~0.48-0.52 full height, so no defect is recorded. If it is a crack, the reference shows no such line and the observed line is an anomaly under GB-2/GB-3.
proposed_action.rationale: Cheapest discriminating check: a reference comparison directly tests the GB-1 criterion (seam present on reference at same place) with no robot motion. It is the recommended check in PROC-GB-001.

candidates.expected_evidence: Reference includes the centre-line seam (supports seam, no defect) versus reference lacks the line (supports crack or other anomaly).

candidates.hypothesis: Cast shadow from the left light or a fixture (shadow moves with light) vs. a real surface feature (stays fixed on the part).

hypotheses_addressed: cast shadow from an edge or fixture
proposed_action.expected_evidence: If the line is a cast shadow from the left light, it shifts or disappears under right or diffuse light. If it is a surface feature (seam or crack), it stays at x~0.5 on the part under the new light.
proposed_action.rationale: Changing lighting from the front pose is a cheap test that separates shadows from surface features, as the technique note prescribes. Right light is chosen because the left-light gradient suggests a left-side source, so a right light should move a shadow noticeably. The line's persistence under a second light also feeds the GB-3 'stays in place under two lights' criterion.

candidates.expected_evidence: Shadow hypothesis: line moves or vanishes. Surface feature hypothesis: line remains at the same location on the part.

candidates.hypothesis: Crack with a raised or broken edge (bright lip under raking light/oblique view) vs. a flat seam or printed/stain mark with no relief.

hypotheses_addressed: expected mold seam or flat mark
proposed_action.expected_evidence: A crack with a broken edge shows a bright reflective lip or gap along the line in the oblique view. A mold seam or printed mark shows no bright edge and stays dark and uniform.
proposed_action.rationale: A low oblique view exaggerates relief, which is the GB-3 bright-edge test for a check. It is a single camera move that does not depend on the lighting result, so it gives independent evidence about whether the line has surface relief.

candidates.expected_evidence: Bright edge or gap along the line supports crack; uniform dark line with no edge supports seam or flat mark.
